card: A motorcycle safety app. Core feature: crash detection with an automatic emergency SMS.
This video shows how the SEND_SMS permission is explained, refused, allowed and used.
Real screen recordings of two phones: the rider's and the emergency contact's. Waiting times are cut, no step is removed, fast parts are marked ×4 ×8 ×10 ×16. No sound. Personal data is blurred.
Step 1 was filmed last (20:40), after removing the SMS permission. Steps 2–9 are one take filmed before it (20:16–20:32).

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: SMS permission: refuse, then allow
subs: The rider opens MotoRoute from the phone's home screen.
The red SOS button sits in the header; crash detection is in the Route tab.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: SMS permission: refuse, then allow
subs: Route tab → My emergencies.
SMS permission not granted (removed before this recording): nothing can be sent automatically.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE · ZOOM
segments.title: SMS permission: refuse, then allow
sub: Before Android asks anything, MotoRoute explains in its own window what the SMS permission is used for (full text, enlarged).

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: SMS permission: refuse, then allow
subs: The rider taps “Not now”…
…Android's permission screen is NOT opened and SMS stays NOT allowed.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: SMS permission: refuse, then allow
subs: Later, the rider taps “Allow SMS” again…
…and this time taps “I agree”.
Android's own prompt (phone set to French): “Allow MotoRoute to send and view SMS?”
This is Android's standard wording for the SMS group. MotoRoute requests SEND_SMS only.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: SMS permission: refuse, then allow
subs: The rider taps “Autoriser” (Allow).
Emergency SMS allowed. The rider can revoke this permission at any time in Android settings.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: Emergency card and consent
sub: Steps 2–9: one take, filmed before Step 1 (20:16–20:32). The card was emptied first; SMS was already allowed.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE · ×8
segments.title: Emergency card and consent
sub: The rider types a name and blood type (shown 8× faster).

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE · ZOOM
segments.title: Emergency card and consent
subs: The blood type is sent ONLY if the rider ticks this consent box. It is unticked by default…
…here the rider ticks it.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE · ×10
segments.title: Emergency card and consent
sub: One emergency contact: name and phone number (shown 10× faster).

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: Emergency card and consent
subs: The rider ticks “I told this contact they may receive my MotoRoute alerts”, then saves.
Card saved: Rider · blood type O+ · Test contact (number blurred).

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: Test SMS started by the rider
subs: The rider taps “Test the SMS”…
…and MotoRoute asks for confirmation before sending.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: Test SMS started by the rider
subs: The rider taps OK: one test SMS (“MotoRoute test SMS…”) to the saved number.
Sent and confirmed by the network.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: Test SMS started by the rider
sub: Delivery confirmed by the operator's delivery report.

segments.label: CONTACT'S PHONE
segments.title: Test SMS started by the rider
sub: On the contact's phone: the test SMS, received at 20:21.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: Crash detection: off by default
subs: Automatic crash detection is OFF by default. The rider turns it on…
…detection only runs while MotoRoute is open (e.g. phone on the handlebar mount).

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: Crash detected: the rider can cancel
subs: “Simulate a crash” (hidden test button) runs the real alert flow.
Crash detected: alarm and a 2-minute countdown (no sound in this video).

segments.title: Crash detected: the rider can cancel

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: Crash detected: the rider can cancel
subs: The rider taps “I'm fine — cancel”…
…and nothing is sent.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: No answer for 2 minutes: one SMS
sub: Second simulation: this time the rider does not answer.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE · ×16
segments.title: No answer for 2 minutes: one SMS

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: No answer for 2 minutes: one SMS
sub: SOS triggered: ONE SMS to the saved number, with name, blood type (consent given) and GPS position.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE · ZOOM
segments.title: No answer for 2 minutes: one SMS
subs: SOS triggered: ONE SMS to the saved number, with name, blood type (consent given) and GPS position.
Sent (confirmed by the network), labelled TEST in test mode, and delivered.

segments.label: CONTACT'S PHONE
segments.title: The contact receives the position
sub: Received at 20:26: “MotoRoute SOS: TEST not a real crash…” with the GPS position (blurred here).

segments.label: CONTACT'S PHONE
segments.title: The contact receives the position
sub: The contact taps the position in the SMS…

segments.label: CONTACT'S PHONE
segments.title: The contact receives the position

segments.title: False alarm: no automatic SMS
subs: The rider taps “False alarm – cancel sending”.
No automatic SMS: MotoRoute only offers “Tell my contact I'm OK” (an alert SMS already went out).

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: False alarm: no automatic SMS
subs: The rider taps “Tell my contact I'm OK”…
…Android asks which SMS app to use: MotoRoute does not send this message itself.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: False alarm: no automatic SMS
sub: The rider's own SMS app opens with a pre-filled message. MotoRoute's earlier SMS show there too: nothing is hidden.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: False alarm: no automatic SMS
sub: Sent by the rider from their own SMS app, not by MotoRoute.

segments.label: CONTACT'S PHONE
segments.title: False alarm: no automatic SMS
subs: Three SMS in total on the contact's phone: test (20:21), alert (20:26), and the rider's own “I'm fine” (20:30).
Nothing at 20:24: the alert cancelled in Step 5 sent nothing.

segments.label: RIDER'S PHONE
segments.title: Turned off in one tap
subs: Route tab → Crash detection: the rider turns it off…
…in one tap. While it is off, no alert SMS can be sent.

card: SEND_SMS is used for two things only

1 · The automatic crash alert: ONE SMS to each number the rider saved (2 max), after 2 minutes without an answer. In this video it is started by the hidden test button “Simulate a crash”: same flow, SMS labelled TEST.
2 · The test SMS (“MotoRoute test SMS…”) that the rider starts and confirms.
MotoRoute never reads, receives or stores SMS. After a false alarm, nothing is sent automatically.
